entry.title: Combined summary - PQ-single-address-backup - BIP-38 for P2MR (bc1z) - 104-char encrypted backup format
entry.summary: The discussion revolves around the development of a secure method for storing cryptographic seeds, specifically for use with Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) 360. The focus is on creating a format that enhances the safety and utility of offline cold storage or inheritance solutions for cryptocurrency keys. The proposed solution involves an encrypted single-address backup system, named PQ-single-address-backup (SAB), which aligns with BIP-360 but does not alter its foundational definitions. This backup system uses a Base58 encoding scheme to handle a payload consisting of various cryptographic elements including a salt, initialization vector (IV), ciphertext, and authentication tag. This results in a strictly defined format that maintains a fixed length of 104 characters. To ensure compatibility and future-proofing, the format excludes specific prefixes like `bc1z`/`bc1r` to remain adaptable with the evolution of BIP-360. The seed itself remains a pure 32-byte SLH-DSA type, ensuring robust security practices while maintaining simplicity in implementation. The encryption method specified includes PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for key derivation and AES-256-GCM for encryption, providing strong protection against unauthorized access while allowing for effective auditability due to the deterministic output length and composition. The design seeks to address several technical and usability challenges associated with long-term storage of cryptographic seeds. This includes defining clear recovery user experiences, such as the implementation of checksums for typo detection prior to running the Key Derivation Function (KDF), and explicit feedback mechanisms for incorrect password entries or unsupported versions. The strategy also emphasizes maintaining a fixed 104-character length for the backup to facilitate ease of scanning and visual verification, which is crucial for ensuring integrity and ease of use during critical recovery scenarios. On the technical side, discussions highlighted the need for a self-describing payload which would enable wallets to accurately interpret the data without relying solely on external or human-readable hints that could be ignored by decoders. This approach would help in managing different versions and profiles in the future, ensuring that the backup system remains robust against technological evolution and varying implementations. Additionally, considerations are being made to include KDF parameters within an outer header of the backup format, which would be treated as Associated Encrypted Data (AAD) to allow for secure selection and verification of the decryption procedure before processing the encrypted payload. The repository hosting the ongoing development and specifications of this project can be accessed at [GitHub](https://github.com/coldtest-berlin/pq-single-address-backup) and a live demonstration is available at [Live Demo](https://coldtest-berlin.github.io/pq-single-address-backup). The community's involvement is sought to further refine these proposals and integrate them into a shared Bitcoin Improvement Proposal if there is significant interest and consensus on the approach.
